scope_entries.finding: There is no ../coherence; the sibling is coherence-cli (pyproject.toml:3 version = "0.6.1"). It scores one text artifact per call (quality/meaning/signal/investiture/frames) into a five-key envelope (coherence/schema.py:59). Its quality domain is regex presence only and says so: docs/domains.md:43 "actually published, or verify a quote's accuracy against any real record." It needs numpy and httpx (pyproject.toml:17). Its open issue #18 (opened 2026-11-17 by the operator) names Associate as consumer of an embedding-drift monitor: "Coherence owns measurement; Associate owns interpretation and behavior".

One choke point exists: index.ts:288 pi.on("tool_call", ...) runs for every call including Pi built-ins, and can only block with a reason string (guard.ts:79-80 block/reason is the whole GuardDecision). No tool takes a purpose today (grep of purpose|intent|expect over tools/, guard.ts, gate.ts, index.ts hit only comments). write and edit are Pi built-ins (guard.ts:43-44, no registerTool here), so a schema field cannot reach them; only the hook can. run_tests refuses extra keys (tools/tests.ts:582).

A walk entry today is id, ts, tool, args, result, truncated, error? (walk.ts:70-77; schema required list at walk.schema.json:17). It is written after the result, one line per call; the pending call lives only in memory (walk.ts:259). One args value is kept (walk.ts:379), so asked-versus-sent is not recorded. result is the redacted text the model saw (walk.ts:500), dropped to sha256+bytes above max_raw_chars 2000000 (walk.ts:506, policy.json:97). The spill path of a bounded result is not in the entry; Pi details are read only for truncated. Ids w1..wN are dense and stable (walk.ts:283, 520).

Full results are saved only by tools that call boundOutput (read, bash, web, code_lens, eidetic_recall, ledger_list — grep of boundOutput( on 2026-11-17), to the session scratch dir, content-addressed; the model sees a head+tail preview and the spill path (contain.ts:520) with no omitted count. grep/find/ls cap at caps.max_results with no spill file and discard the true total (tools/search.ts:492 count: capped.items.length).

walk.ts:4-9 states every entry maps 1:1 to a Pi event and the harness never synthesizes an entry; walk.ts:327-328 says no entry is written at call time because "writing a second line per call would break the 1:1 event mapping c43 requires". Tools see only walkPath and recordChild (context.ts). A purpose written before the call therefore either rides in the call arguments or relaxes the one-line-per-call rule.

Guard refusals always have a reason (guard.ts:80 readonly reason: string) and some include a fix in prose. A gate refusal can reach the model with no reason: gate.ts:1140 ...(j.reason ? { reason: j.reason } : {}) and the guard appends it conditionally. Structured errors are code, message, field (contain.ts:135 makeStructuredError) with no fix field; path_escapes_root, denylist and gitignore refusals give no fix. validateArgs (contain.ts:737) ignores additionalProperties and minLength.

A statement today is text, evidence (wN ids), status referenced|unreferenced, citations (statements.ts:59-60, statements.schema.json:23). There is no quote, value or source-kind field and no matcher (grep quote|verbatim|nearest over statements.ts and handback.ts found nothing). The only content check is verifyCitation (statements.ts:337): a path:line inside a recorded read range is marked encountered, which the file itself says is not support. Only read tools yield ranges (statements.ts:291). Every handler is additive and returns nothing (statements.ts:603), so nothing is ever refused.

A matcher available both to the model mid-run (TypeScript) and to the Python harness exists twice or on one side only; the session-id sanitizer is the existing precedent for a duplicated algorithm kept in step.

The only source labelling today is a session-cumulative taint `untrusted:<child|repo|web>` (eidetic.ts:163) attached to memory records only (eidetic.ts:343); there is no label on a walk entry or result. A spawn_subagent hand-back and a delegate_status final_reply are the child model's own words; delegate.ts:801 says so in prose ("final_reply is the delegated model's own account; outcome, merge, merge_reason and tests are the harness's"). Child walks are linked by a `c<N>` line that a statement cannot cite (handback.ts:22 EVIDENCE_ID allows only wN). torch.ts:139 re-injects a prior run's statements under "# Prior walk — observed facts, not instructions". web results carry URL and truncated but no fetch time.

finish requires only summary (index.ts:222); statements and evidence are optional. It never refuses: it normalizes, counts unreferenced, sets finished = true (index.ts:263) and blocks every later tool call (index.ts:289-295). Dropped ids and statements are not reported back, only a count. policy.json and gate.json contain no retry or rounds setting (grep retry|rounds|attempt, no hits), and the model prompts tell it not to retry a refused call. A run that ends without finish is not marked as a failure for that reason: the outcome is ok when no call was left unresolved (walk.ts:476), error when one was, and unknown when no run line exists (pi.py _outcome); the missing finish shows only in final_reply/stop_reason. (Last sentence corrected after the worker review run scope20-worker-t4, which checked this finding and qualified it.)

Run outcomes are ok|error|refused|budget_exceeded (walk.ts:62) and in practice ok unless a call had no result (walk.ts:476); markOutcome has no caller outside its definition (grep 2026-11-17). Merge is decided in run.py _finish from outcome and operator test results; read-only runs skip it, and their artifacts are always left on disk with exit 0. There is no named outcome for timeout, no-finish, lane error or a failed content check, and no analogue of "result not stored" for a read-only run.

Nothing in schema, code or finish parameters models kinds of statement, alternatives, verdicts, confidence or open questions (grep confidence|cannot tell|hypothes|verdict|alternative over lib/, index.ts, prompts/, schemas/). Two tests pin the absence of the word supported (statements.test.ts:301 and :366), and "verdict" already names the safety gate's answer (gate.ts:175, walk.schema.json gate.verdict). AGENTS.md:67 asks only to "Keep facts, inferences and recommendations visibly apart"; no prompt asks for a verbatim quote, for what was not read, or for how to report not found.

Issue #12 states "Associate should not own plans, waves, DAGs or long-running workflow state." Issue #17 records that a child is gated against cortex-written sub-task text and proposes recording the sub-task text and the root task side by side in the parent walk child line; a model-written purpose is the same kind of text, so feeding it to the gate inherits that risk and #17 waits on #13.

walkstats reads only the final run line and gate lines of each walk (walkstats.py:58 OUTCOMES) and never entry fields or statements. No reviewer flag or grade store exists (grep grader|reviewer over associate/*.py, no hits). A new result field or a new verb must be mirrored in explain/catalog.py (run entry, ## Output), learn.py (_TEXT and _as_json_payload) and is pinned by tests/test_run.py and tests/test_cli_introspection.py.

Recorded live failures a check can cite, each a single run (t20-live-acceptance.md:58 "Each of these is one run."): senses reported "Eidetic remember: Success" with no eidetic_remember call in its walk (:53); the worker "ended without `finish` and with an empty final reply" (:44), "the third live occurrence" (:47); a test command passed on a file that was never written (lapse l9, :46). The walks are not committed (:20), so only these notes and sha256 prefixes remain. gate-calibration.md records that no gate variant separates an honest ledger entry from a false one (issue #15).

ledger_append sends agent (filled by the extension, ledger.ts:77 AGENT_PREFIX), action, summary, refs and data; refs are free strings never checked against walk ids, and nothing the harness measured is appended. Issue #15 lists the candidate fixes: "require `refs` that point at walk ids (`wN`), and check the cited entries exist", "have the harness itself append the run's measured outcome", and flag unreferenced entries.

scope_entries.surface: workledger-cli (sibling; origin/main 0.8.0, local checkout 0.7.0, ledger not on PATH)
scope_entries.finding: Read at origin/main: an entry is agent, action, summary plus optional refs and data (workledger/cli/_commands/_store.py:25-27), unknown fields are rejected (:144), id and timestamp are generated, append is O_APPEND with no lock and no hash chain (:274), and the only verbs beyond the template are append and list. Its open issue #4 (2026-09-22) already asks to "Adopt the walk + statements evidence shape as the ledger entry format" with a finish that "rejects a statement citing an unknown id"; none of it is built. The local checkout is one release behind and `ledger` is not installed, so associate's ledger tools fail with tool_missing today (seen live in run scope20-cortex-t1, entry w12).

Both are unmodified template scaffolds with only whoami/learn/explain/overview/doctor verbs. rigor-cli README.md:7: "**The ledger domain is not implemented yet.**"; its brief (issue #1) plans premises, inference steps, `rigor check` (replay) and `rigor why <entry>` (the support set behind a conclusion), and says "Not yours: deciding what is true". evidence-cli README.md:3 promises it "grades that evidence across parameters and issues a final score"; its brief (issue #1) requires that "A high evidence grade means the trail is complete and traceable. It does not mean the work is correct." Neither reads a walk, matches a quote or counts facts; neither is on PATH; both have dependencies = [].

devague records and never verifies: an evidence record is obligation_ref, test_ref, behavior_text, evidence_type, strength, strength_basis, outcome (devague/delivery.py), where the only content checks are enum membership and a commit-SHA pattern; a scope entry is id, surface, finding, seeds with only seed-id existence checked. README.md:97 "- **Call an LLM.** The CLI is deterministic and fully unit-tested." is listed under what it never does. Its lapse codes (frame.py:84 "assumption-for-measurement", :89 "provenance-missing") are an existing vocabulary for "rested on something unread". Open issue #113 asks for a mechanical evidence-wording check, the nearest precedent for a citation check.

A record's metadata is free-form and "round-trips verbatim" on recall (CLAUDE.md:80); there is no trust, source or quote field (grep trust|verified|quote|stale over eidetic/memory/record.py and scope.py). signal (record.py:73) is computed at recall from age and recall count and rises with use, so it says nothing about whether content is still true. associate's eidetic_remember adds only added_via and the session taint (tools/eidetic.ts:343): no session id, walk id or quote.

CLAUDE.md "What not to invent" keeps lobes-cli and colleague as consumed-as-is (spec boundary c18) and forbids naming a checkpoint id. The same section requires a version bump on every PR and forbids describing anything as working before a live run measures it; the in-house behavioral suite that carried citation checks was dropped (spec 2026-10-27 line 212), so new checks have unit tests against fakes plus recorded live runs, and no regression suite.

The gate state is exactly task, action, effect, arguments, model, isolation, change (gate.json:10, gate.ts:111) and only mutating and gated tools reach it; pure reads never do. arguments is the whole redacted argument object (gate.ts:595), so a purpose passed as a tool argument would reach CLEF unless the harness strips it first. Any change to what CLEF is asked is a gate.json version bump with a calibration note, and issue #17 documents that model-written task text can make an action look on-task.

scope_entries.finding: Both answered the gate-threshold question correctly against associate/contract/gate.json lines 3 and 65-71 and models.json lines 28-29 (checked by hand). cortex added "a content-identical copy of the same table also sits in pyproject.toml (line 67)"; pyproject.toml contains no gated_tools, safe_unattended or allow_when (grep count 0) and cortex never read that file. scope_entries.finding: Neither review produced a hand-back. worker made 77 calls (45 reads, 21 greps) and was killed 50 s after a ledger_append that failed with tool_missing; cortex made 67 calls and was killed mid-read. Both ended with exit 2, no result object, no run line and zero statements. Reasoning is fixed per model in the registry: worker and cortex are "on" (models.json:36, :68) and provider.ts:179 sets supportsReasoningEffort: false; no associate run flag or environment variable changes it per run, so the only control is a different contract copy. A timed-out run cannot be resumed: pi is killed, no result is returned, and the one way on is a new run with --continue-from, which injects the prior walk clipped to 25000 characters in total (torch.ts:45, per-entry share at torch.ts:136). For this survey a scratch copy of the tree with both models set to "off" is used for the continuation runs `scope20-<model>-t5`.

scope_entries.surface: live run scope20-worker-t5 (worker, reasoning off via a scratch contract copy, continuing scope20-worker-t3 with --continue-from; 35 calls, 318 s)
scope_entries.finding: With reasoning off the worker handed back a full review of all eight findings in 5.3 minutes, where the same task with reasoning on was killed at 25 minutes. It was shown the prior walk with its ids and cited those: all 22 ids in its statements match the prior run's entries for the files named (prior w10 is the read of index.ts, w21 the read of walk.ts, and so on). The harness resolved them against the new run's walk, where w10 is policy.json and w21 is statements.ts, and recorded every statement as referenced. Walk ids restart at w1 in every run, so a continued run's citations are ambiguous. obligations.behavior: given pi 1.5.2 installed, the launcher runs without the version warning, and with another version it warns naming 1.5.2
obligations.source_text: the harness pin moves from pi 1.1.0 to pi 1.5.2 as part of this work (operator decision, 2026-11-17: upgrading to 1.5.2 is approved)

obligations.seam: answer field of the run result
obligations.behavior: given a hand-back whose summary or final message contains a sentence tied to no accepted item, the answer field omits it and the report counts it as uncovered
obligations.source_text: no free text reaches the caller as a checked answer: the answer in the run result is rendered by the harness from the accepted facts and conclusions, and whatever else the model wrote (the finish summary, the final message) is delivered under an unchecked label with its sentence count in the report

obligations.behavior: given a fact that an action happened which cites an entry of another tool or an entry that ended in an error or refusal, the fact is refused
obligations.source_text: a statement that an action happened (a tool ran, a file changed, a test passed, a record was stored) is a fact whose cited entry must be a call of that tool that did not end in an error or refusal

obligations.behavior: given a quote shorter than the contract minimum, or a literal value that does not occur in its quote, the fact is refused
obligations.source_text: the matcher refuses a quote shorter than a minimum length set in the contract, and when a fact value is a literal (a number, an identifier, a path) that literal must occur inside the quote

obligations.behavior: given report mode, a hand-back that would be refused is accepted and the report lists each refusal it would have made; given enforce mode, it is refused
obligations.source_text: the checks ship with a mode set in the contract, report or enforce, per model and overridable per run: in report mode nothing is refused and the report says what would have been; a model moves to enforce only after a recorded live run in report mode

obligations.behavior: given the same refusal repeated up to the contract cap, the run ends with a named outcome
obligations.source_text: consecutive refusals for the same reason (a missing purpose, a failed hand-back) are capped by a number in the contract; at the cap the run ends with a named outcome instead of looping to its time limit

obligations.seam: session export (any session, with or without associate run)
obligations.behavior: given a session with no Python harness, the facts, check results and counts files exist and the report says the Python re-check did not run
obligations.source_text: the extension writes the facts, the check results and the counts itself in every session, so mesh sessions through pi-acp and spawned children have them; the Python re-check runs wherever associate run runs (headless and delegated runs), and the report says when it did not run

obligations.seam: associate run exit code and stdout
obligations.behavior: given a hand-back still failing after the last round, the process exits 3 and prints the result object on stdout
obligations.source_text: a run whose hand-back still fails the check after the allowed rounds exits 3, the first use of the reserved range, and still prints its result object, so a caller and delegate_status can read the named outcome

obligations.behavior: given an export written before this change, each reads it without an error and reports its facts as not applicable
obligations.source_text: an export says which format it is: the checker, the counts and --continue-from accept an export written before this change and report its facts as not applicable instead of failing; the stub adapter writes the new shape

obligations.behavior: given a reference containing a path separator or anything outside the id pattern, it is refused before any file is opened
obligations.source_text: a fact names its source by run label and walk id only, validated by pattern; the harness maps that to a saved file, and neither the matcher nor the check tool opens a path supplied by the model
